title: Спортивная сумка и вызов на пробежку  (The Gym Bag and the Jogging Challenge)

segments.t: Hungover after celebrating his birthday, Chef Barinov steps out of his apartment building and runs into his neighbor and culinary rival, Elena Pavlovna, carrying a large gym bag. When Elena claims she has been working out and challenges him to a morning jog in the park tomorrow, Viktor Petrovich stubbornly accepts.
Уж не скажете ли вы, что занимаетесь спортом?
А может, мы с вами вместе побегаем?
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Happy birthday.' Underscoring the birth at once, Barinov uses "rozhdeniya" ("of birth", from "rozhdeniye") to make the point stick.
'Maybe I should give you some pills?' Mentioning the pill in the exchange, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'There is no need.' Rodion fires back honestly in this moment, leaving no doubt about where he stands.

'Good morning, Viktor Petrovich.' Vika readily offers this morning greeting for Barinov using "dobroye utro" ("good morning") — literally "kind morning", with the neuter ending matching "utro" ("morning").
'Rodion Sergeyevich.' Cutting in calmly in front of Rodion, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Should I suggest where to hide the body?' Rodion prompts skeptically before Barinov can change the subject.
Уж не скажете ли вы, что занимаетесь спортом?
'You are not going to tell me that you play sports, are you?' Touching on the sport at once, Barinov centers the thought on "zanimayetes" ("are busy with", from "zanimatsya") without wasting a word.
'Do you doubt it?' Looking over directly before Barinov, the "-sya" ending on "somnevayetes" ("to doubt") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'I have no doubts.' Rodion continues sharply with a shrug, bringing things back to earth after the buildup.
'You do not say?' Barinov cuts in naturally during the talk and brings in "govorite" ("say, speak", from "govorit") as the key Russian word here.
А может, мы с вами вместе побегаем?

'Maybe the two of us should go jogging together?' Cutting in plainly in this beat, Vika keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Rodion purely through rising pitch.
'We will go for a run first thing tomorrow.' Rodion chimes in candidly with a smile, without trying to dress up how he really feels.
'Right here in the park.' Emphasizing the park right here, Barinov reaches for the Russian word "parke" ("park", built from "park") right at the center of the line.
Уж не скажете ли вы, что занимаетесь спортом?
А может, мы с вами вместе побегаем?

That wraps up this scene as after a wild birthday party at his apartment, Chef Barinov meets rival chef Elena carrying a gym bag and impulsively agrees to go jogging with her in the park tomorrow morning. Until next time!
